name: Qwixx

key_numbers.label: Crosses needed before locking a row

setup.text: Put the six dice in the middle.
Take a score sheet and something to write with.
The first player to roll a 6 is the first active player.

turn.summary: The active player rolls all dice. Everyone may mark the white sum; then only the active player may mark a white plus coloured die.
steps: Roll all six dice and say the total of the two white dice. Everyone, you included, may cross out that number in one row of any colour.
Then only the active player may add one white die to one coloured die and cross out that sum in the row of that colour.
If the active player crosses nothing in either step, they cross a penalty box.
You must cross numbers left to right in each row. Skipped numbers can never be crossed later.

round_end: The player to the left becomes active and rolls all the remaining dice.
end: The game ends at once when someone crosses a fourth penalty box or when two rows have been locked (two dice removed). A third row may lock at the same time as the second.

scoring.text: For each row, count crosses (including a lock) and score: 1 cross 1, 2 crosses 3, 3 crosses 6, 4 crosses 10, 5 crosses 15, 6 crosses 21, 7 crosses 28, 8 crosses 36, 9 crosses 45, 10 crosses 55, 11 crosses 66, 12 crosses 78.
Subtract 5 for each crossed penalty box. The highest total wins.

missed.text: To cross the far-right number (red 12, yellow 12, green 2, blue 2) you must already have five crosses in that row.
Crossing that number also lets you cross the lock. The row is closed for everyone and its die is removed immediately.
The lock counts as a cross when scoring.
Only the active player takes penalties; others never do for passing.
If a row is locked in the first action, other players can lock the same row at the same time if they have five crosses.

unverified: Row direction (red and yellow rising to 12, green and blue falling to 2) is inferred from the lock numbers and colour list because the printed rows are partly icons.
Tie-break is not stated in the rulebook text.
